1.tell: fifths ladder -2/5,4/5,6/5,10/5; no clean hub. 4/5 sits so that 6/5 = +2/5 and -2/5 = -(2/5) off it; guessed the centre-ish fraction

2.tell: 15 and 8 are the two ingredients, 23 = 15+8 and 120 = 15*8. Set is 'two parts + their sum + their product' — the sum is the usual ask, the parts and the product are the standard distractors

3.tell: perfect ±4/±16 quad with 16 = 4^2, fully symmetric so no hub. Chose the negative small root: a sign-trap quad is built when the true answer is negative

4.tell: 12,16,20 arithmetic (step 4) with 15 outside; 16 is the centre of the ladder

5.tell: 64 is the hub: 64*3 = 192 and 64 = 4^3, so it touches all three others; 192 and 4 and 3 do not touch each other except through it

6.tell: 15,20,25 arithmetic (step 5) plus 16; 20 is the centre of the ladder

7.tell: 5 is a clean centre: -5 (sign flip), 7 (+2), 3 (-2). Every distractor is one edit from 5 and none is an edit from another

8.tell: ±2/±8 with 8 = 2^3, symmetric. Read as a cube/odd-root item: -2 generates 2 (sign), -8 and 8 (cube). Negative small value chosen for the same sign-trap reason as item 3

10.tell: ±2/±5 symmetric quad, no hub at all. Coin flip biased to the negative small value

11.tell: 20, 21.25, 22.5, 25: the three round values are the ladder, 21.25 is the one unround value and the only one you cannot reach by halving/averaging round numbers by accident

12.tell: 3,4 with their squares 9,16. 4 is the hub — 16 is its square-error partner and 3/9 the off-by-one pair

13.tell: 49/4 = (7/2)^2 and also sits on the 33/4, 41/4, 49/4 quarter-ladder, so it is the only value touching both families — completing-the-square shape

14.tell: 7/2 is a textbook centre: 2/7 (reciprocal), 7/3 (denominator slip), 3/2 (numerator slip). All three are one token-edit from it and none from each other

15.tell: 28,32,36 step-4 ladder with 44 outside; 32 is the centre

16.tell: 8 is the centre: 16 (double), 4 (half), 6 (-2). Classic double/halve/off-by satellite set

17.tell: 13500 is exactly half of 27000 — the 'forgot to double' distractor — which makes 27000 the parent value; 24000 and 16000 are round decoys

19.tell: 5 carries the sign twin (-5) and 7 = 5+2, 1 = 5-4; the value with a sign partner is the parent

20.tell: 4 and 9 are squares and 13 = 4+9, so 13 is the value the others compose into; 10 is a near-miss decoy

21.tell: 4 holds the sign twin (-4); 5 = 4+1 and 10 is the doubling decoy. Weak — 5 could equally be the parent with 10 as its double

22.tell: 6 is the hub: -6 (sign), 24 (times 4), 9 (+3). Only 6 touches all three

23.tell: 85 and 100 are the round input-looking values; between the two computed values 106.80 reads as the compounding result and 98.89 as the wrong-order/decay variant

24.tell: in quarters: 10, 12, 13, 14. 3 (=12/4) is the midpoint of 5/2 and 7/2 and 13/4 is the midpoint of 3 and 7/2 — took the symmetric centre
